question: Who said a life without examination isn't worth living, and at what point in the trial?
answer_notes: Socrates, in the penalty speech, explaining why he cannot just keep quiet in exile: daily talk about virtue is the greatest good, and the unexamined life is not worth living.

question: Which passage has Socrates calling himself the gadfly of Athens?
answer_notes: God gave him to the city like a gadfly to a big, sluggish horse, to rouse it; if they kill him they will not easily find another (039 continues the image).

question: Where does Socrates say he is wiser only because he doesn't imagine he knows what he doesn't?
answer_notes: After questioning a politician: the man knows nothing and thinks he knows; Socrates neither knows nor thinks he knows, so he has a slight advantage.

question: How does the speech end, the line about him going off to die and the jurors going on to live?
answer_notes: The closing words: the hour of departure has come, he goes to die and they to live, and which is better only God knows.

question: Where does Socrates tell the jury he will obey the god rather than them?
answer_notes: If they freed him on condition he stop philosophising, he would refuse: he honours and loves them but will obey God, and never stop practising philosophy.

question: Who said that nothing bad can happen to a good man, alive or dead?
answer_notes: Socrates to the jurors who voted to acquit: be of good cheer about death; no evil can happen to a good man in life or after death.

question: Where is the line that wickedness is harder to escape than death because it runs faster?
answer_notes: The difficulty is not to avoid death but unrighteousness, which runs faster; he, old and slow, was caught by death, his quick accusers by wickedness.

question: Where does Socrates borrow Homer's words to say he isn't made of wood or stone?
answer_notes: Explaining why he won't bring his family to beg: he is flesh and blood, 'not of wood or stone' as Homer says, and has three sons, yet won't use them to plead.

question: What did the priestess reply when his friend asked whether anybody surpassed Socrates in wisdom?
answer_notes: Chaerephon asked the oracle at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates; the prophetess said no one was. 011 has Socrates puzzling over what the god meant.

question: Why won't Socrates parade his family before the jury to win their pity?
answer_notes: Begging with tearful relatives would disgrace himself, the jurors and the city; men with a reputation for wisdom should not demean themselves 048 adds that begging would ask the judges to break their oath.

question: What did Socrates learn when he tested people who work with their hands?
answer_notes: The artisans did know many things he didn't, but, like the poets, thought this made them experts on the highest matters too; he judged himself better off as he was.

question: Do the authors of plays and verse understand their own works, according to Socrates?
answer_notes: No: poets compose by a kind of inspiration, like diviners, saying fine things without understanding them, and then think themselves wise in other matters as well.

question: What does Socrates propose the city give him in place of a punishment?
answer_notes: As a poor benefactor who spent his life urging people towards virtue, he deserves free meals in the Prytaneum, more than an Olympic victor.

question: Why does Socrates refuse to accept banishment as his sentence?
answer_notes: If his own citizens can't bear his talk, strangers won't either; he would be driven from city to city, and the young would follow him wherever he went.

question: What is the private divine warning Socrates has had since boyhood, and what does it do?
answer_notes: A sign or voice that only ever holds him back, never urges; it kept him out of politics (040). In 058 it stayed silent all day, which he takes to mean his death is a good.

question: What did Socrates do when the oligarchs ordered him to help seize a man for execution?
answer_notes: Under the Thirty he was told, with four others, to fetch Leon of Salamis to be killed; the others went, he went home, and might have died for it.

question: When Socrates served on the city council, how did he stand against an unlawful group trial?
answer_notes: As one of the Prytanes he alone opposed trying the generals of Arginusae together, against the law, despite threats of arrest and death.

question: Did Socrates ever earn a living from his conversations?
answer_notes: No: he denies taking money for teaching (007), his poverty is proof that he never sought pay (039), and he talks with rich and poor alike (043).

question: Why does Socrates not fear death?
answer_notes: Fearing death is pretending to know what no one knows; it may be the greatest good (034). His divine sign didn't oppose him (058); death is either dreamless sleep or a journey to the other world (059); no evil comes to a good man (061).

question: What does Socrates think might happen to us after we die?
answer_notes: Two possibilities: nothingness, like a sleep without dreams, which would be a gain; or a migration of the soul, where he could meet the heroes and poets and keep questioning.

question: Does Socrates claim to know more than everyone else, and if not, what gives him the edge?
answer_notes: Only in knowing that he does not know; the god uses him as an example that human wisdom is worth little. 034 repeats this about death.

question: Why did Socrates never take up a career in government?
answer_notes: His divine sign held him back, and anyone who honestly fights injustice in public life would be killed; he did more good talking to people privately.

question: What does Socrates think people should prioritize in life?
answer_notes: The soul's improvement, wisdom and truth over money, reputation and the body; virtue isn't produced by money, but money and every other good come from virtue.

question: Why does Socrates believe his accusers cannot truly hurt him?
answer_notes: A worse man cannot harm a better one; killing him unjustly harms the killers more (037). No evil can happen to a good man (061).

question: Why is Socrates so widely disliked in Athens?
answer_notes: His questioning exposes people who think they are wise, which makes enemies; young men imitate him, and the exposed blame Socrates and repeat stock charges against philosophers.

question: How does Socrates defend himself against the claim that he is a bad influence on young people?
answer_notes: He shows Meletus has never thought about who improves the young (020, 021); no one would harm the people they live among on purpose (023); none of his young associates' families accuse him (044).

question: What poison was Socrates given when he was executed?
answer_notes: The Apology ends with the death sentence; the hemlock is in the Phaedo. Retrieval will find death passages, but none says how he died.

question: Why did Socrates turn down Crito's plan to help him escape from prison?
answer_notes: That is the Crito. Crito appears in the Apology only as a friend in court (044) and a surety for the fine (054).

question: What did Socrates' wife Xanthippe say during the trial?
answer_notes: His wife is not mentioned; only his three sons (046) and their future (062).

question: What is Plato's theory of Forms?
answer_notes: Not in the Apology. Plato is mentioned only as present in court (045) and offering surety (054).
